feedback.problem:
The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,{x}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $1.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) & =(1)(x-(-5))(x-4) \\  & =(x+5)(x-4)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)(x-4) & ={x}^{2}-4x+5x-20 \\  & ={x}^{2}+x-20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)={x}^{2}+x-20.$
